$comment: Recorded corrections to the 0.6 pin. check-openapi-pin.sh replaces each operation in the pin with `operation` before comparing; see its RECORDED CORRECTIONS header.

operation.description:
Folds one facet row owned by the edge, addressed by the `property_id` the facets read
returned. The row persists as history and the read stops returning it; asserting the same
address again mints a fresh row. Authorizes through the same clauses as the other edge
writes. A property id naming another edge, an unknown one, and an already-retracted one all
answer the same 404.

parameters.description: Relationship edge handle
parameters.name: edge_handle

parameters.description: Facet row id to retract
parameters.name: property_id

parameters.description:
The invocation this act is correlated under (`kb_events.invocation_id`). Optional — a
correlation aid, never a substitute for authn/authz.
parameters.name: invocation_id

parameters.description:
The act-grain thread this write belongs to (`kb_events.correlation_id`). Optional, caller-
minted, provenance-only. Rides independently of `invocation_id` and of authorship.
parameters.name: correlation_id

parameters.description: Free-text reasoning for the act. Authorship field — requires `confidence`. At most 16384 bytes.
parameters.name: reasoning

parameters.description: Graded self-assessed confidence band. Required whenever any other authorship field is set.
parameters.name: confidence

bytes.
parameters.name: rationale

parameters.description:
The persona/role the author acted as. Authorship field — requires `confidence`. At most 256

parameters.description: The model that authored the act. Authorship field — requires `confidence`. At most 256 bytes.
parameters.name: model

404.description: No live facet row with that id on this relationship

410.description: The relationship's source resource was erased while this request was in flight (code RESOURCE_ERASED); answered only to a caller who held standing on it, everyone else gets 403. Reachable only when an erasure commits during the request: the erasure folds every relationship touching the resource, so a later request answers 404

operation.summary: Retract one facet of a relationship

corrections.reason: The pin declared ActInput's seven fields in: path with no placeholder to fill; the handler has always read them from the query string (Query<ActInput>), so no client could send them as pinned.
corrections.register_row: `ActInput`'s authorship fields are documented as query parameters on all four routes that take them

operation.description:
One gate, two arms, inside the strike's own transaction: delete standing (custody) over
EVERY live relation's resource peer, or — when the blob has no live relations — custody
of its home (a personal context's owner; a team context's owning-team owner role). The
strike empties the row, fires exactly one `blob_deleted`, and folds no edge; when the
struck row was the LAST live row carrying its content hash (`released: true`), the
provider bytes are deleted post-commit and the byte-delete fence retries-and-alerts on
any residue. Already-struck and unknown ids both read 404 with no second event. Author
standing, role, and admin standing confer nothing here — custody alone deletes.

200.description: Struck — the row is emptied and one `blob_deleted` fired; `released` reports whether the provider bytes were this act's to release

403.description: The blob is readable but the caller holds no delete standing over it (custody refusal, `blob_delete:` vocabulary)

404.description: Blob absent, not visible, or already struck — each indistinguishable from absent by design; no second event

operation.summary: Delete one blob — the ordinary delete act's ruled door
